subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — UI dashboard and CLI command

question: Should AI-safety history become a permanent core operator surface, and if so what canonical storage, retention, privacy, and staged landing contract should own it?
rationale: The branch establishes new cross-cutting diagnostics, plugin, gateway, CLI, and UI contracts; choosing their permanent owner and retention policy is product and architecture judgment rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Stage on canonical diagnostics
options.body: Keep the capability in core, but first reuse the established diagnostics projection, persist bounded redacted records in SQLite, and land the stack in an owner-approved sequence.

options.title: Narrow to exporters
options.body: Defer the query store, CLI, and dashboard while separately evaluating the lower-level taxonomy and telemetry exporter contracts.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Pause or close the stacked work until maintainers sponsor a permanent safety taxonomy and operator experience.

recommendation.title: Stage on canonical diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep the capability in core, but first reuse the established diagnostics projection, persist bounded redacted records in SQLite, and land the stack in an owner-approved sequence.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans core product scope, architecture, persistence, security, and the landing sequence rather than one implementation file.
